root.name: Slav Defense: Chebanenko Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 a6

overview: Black plays 4...a6 to prepare ...b5 or ...dxc4 with the bishop still free to leave later via g4 or f5. It is a flexible set-up where Black can choose between a Slav and a Semi-Slav structure depending on White's reply. The usual game is a calm manoeuvring fight with queenside space gains and few forced lines.

white_ideas.idea: Play 5.e3 or 5.Bg5 and keep the centre solid, answering ...b5 with b3 or cxd5.
Play 5.c5 (Advance System) to clamp the queenside and aim for e4.
Use a4 to stop ...b5 and fight for the b5 square.

black_ideas.idea: Play ...b5 and ...Bb7 or ...Bg4 to gain queenside space with a flexible centre.
Choose between ...dxc4 with ...b5 or the Semi-Slav ...e6 set-up once White commits.

typical_structures.structure: Slav pawns c6/d5 with an advanced ...b5 chain on the queenside.
Semi-Slav triangle c6/d5/e6 after ...e6 with the c8-bishop already developed.

character.notes: Black's solid c6/d5 centre with no weak points; sound and rarely forcing.

gambit.notes: No material is offered; ...dxc4 pawns are returned or held without a sacrifice.

soundness.notes: Main-line, respected by strong players including Sveshnikov-era Slav players.

structure.notes: Centre is fixed but not locked; tension c4/d5 stays, pieces and wings decide.

approach.notes: Standard strong-player choice; it avoids the Meran and Botvinnik storms.

level.notes: Clear plans, modest memorisation, moderate positional judgement.

sublines_that_differ.name: Advance System
sublines_that_differ.how: White gains queenside space and plays for e4 and Bf4, a more positional struggle.

character.reason: Compact centre with few ways for Black to lose quickly.

structure.reason: Centre tension undecided; ...dxc4 or ...e6 chosen later.

level.reason: Plans are manageable but need positional judgement.

plans.reason: Black plays ...b5 and keeps the c-file.
